label: The prompt-cost denominator is already paid: AGENTS.md is 300 lines / 27,372 bytes / 27,194 characters, roughly 6,800 tokens resident every turn, so an AGENTS.md mechanism is priced only by its added text.

All five carriers priced in characters: AGENTS.md resident 27,194; its Plan-before-acting bullet 119; a Gate-5-shaped block 978; Gate 3 block 2,422; card total 9,699; card plan-shape section 803; card acceptance+verify pair 178; plan.md.tmpl FILL note 177; advisor brief observed 91 against a 2,048 ceiling; validator registry 15,641 bytes CLI-side; speckit-implement 60,098 bytes and speckit-complete 93,496 bytes per invocation.

Editing an existing AGENTS.md line costs about 30-45 tokens per turn while adding a Gate-shaped block for the same requirement costs 245-606, so the frozen preference for changing an existing line is also the cheapest option by roughly 8x.

The validator mechanism has the only provably zero marginal prompt cost and is the only one that cannot act before implementation: all 42 rules are decidable file-shape or closure checks, none anchors a plan phase to a path or proof command, and the chat path runs validate.sh at completion rather than at the first edit.

The hook's per-turn price is bounded and small (2,048-character brief ceiling, 91-character live brief, per-session dedup) but its reach is six runtime adapters against seven named runtime agent directories, with no .dsh adapter listed.

AGENTS.md is the only carrier this run can prove is present at the first edit, because the delivered prefix of this iteration's own prompt contains the full framework text while SKILL.md, ROUTER.md and the authoring card did not arrive until they were read.

A child with no user present does not inherit sane behaviour from a new gate: the AI_SESSION_CHILD exemption pre-resolves Gate 3 and enumerates exactly the clauses it converts to record-and-continue, so an unnamed gate added later defaults to asking with nobody to answer.

The smallest stopping change is two existing lines in two existing files, each owning one half: AGENTS.md:186 gains the level-qualified, child-qualified pre-implementation review verdict, and the card's 123-124 acceptance+verify pair gains per-phase path-and-proof anchoring, which avoids restating one requirement twice.

Do not build: a new write-gating hook (prompt-time only, six of seven runtimes, new hook concern), a shared step reference file (new file plus pointer cost and ladder restatement), automatic command invocation (15,025-23,374 tokens and 12 confirm checkpoints that need a user), a new numbered Gate block (8x the per-turn price), or another search for a hidden planning-gate enforcer (confirmed absence).

Recommended: mechanism 1, carried by amending the existing AGENTS.md:186 line rather than adding a gate; ranking by marginal per-turn cost crossed with position in the work is M1 > M4 > M3 > M2 > M5, with M4 following as the decidable backstop and explicitly not leading.
A carrier's per-turn price is the delta of text it inserts, never the size of the file that holds it, because the resident files are already in the prompt before any mechanism is chosen.
Any clause added to AGENTS.md must state its AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 behaviour in the same line, since the child-dispatch exemption converts an enumerated clause list and nothing else.

The advisor brief observed in this dispatch is about 91 characters, one seventh of its 2,048-character default ceiling, which bounds the hook mechanism's realistic per-fired-prompt cost to tens of tokens.

Q2's last open input is runtime delivery rather than mechanism design: six advisor adapters are listed against seven runtime agent directories, and whether .devin and .dsh deliver AGENTS.md as a prefix is unevidenced.
